authority: Technical Specification v1.1 is authoritative. Where a phase document fixes a concrete choice the spec left open (names, ports, library picks), that choice is also binding.

R0_test_gate_protocol.title: Test gate protocol
R0_test_gate_protocol.scope: every numbered task in every epic (E0-E8, SIM)
R0_test_gate_protocol.statement: Each numbered task ends in a gate. The entire accumulated test suite must pass before the next task begins. No exceptions, for any reason.
requirements: A gate runs the ENTIRE accumulated suite, not only the new task's tests.
A gate is invoked by exactly one command: `make gate` (`./gate.ps1` on Windows-native shells).
A gate run sets EOE_GATE=1, which makes any skipped, xfailed, or deselected test a hard failure.
Integration tests are part of the gate. Docker is a hard prerequisite, not an optional capability.
The gate result is written to docs/project-updates.md only AFTER it passes and the task's manual verification steps have been run.

forbidden.detail: pytest.mark.skip, pytest.mark.skipif, pytest.mark.xfail, it.skip, test.skip, test.todo, describe.skip, .only
pytest -k, vitest --grep, playwright --grep, --maxfail, --lf, or any filter that narrows the gate suite
known-failure lists, quarantine files, continue-on-error, soft assertions used to downgrade a failure
A test that skips itself when Docker is unavailable is a failing test.

forbidden.action: deleting or weakening a test to clear a gate
forbidden.detail: Requires an explicit docs/DECISIONS.md entry written BEFORE the change.

on_failure: Stop. Do not begin the next task.
Diagnose the root cause. Do not re-run hoping for a different result.
If production code is wrong, fix production code.
If the test is wrong, fix the test AND record the reasoning in docs/DECISIONS.md.
Report the failure to the user verbatim, including the failing output. Never summarize a failure as a pass.

test_critical_suites.note: Spec 14.5 names four components as test-critical. Their suites double as documentation and no later session may weaken them.

R1_record_keeping.title: Project record keeping
R1_record_keeping.boundary: Three logs, non-overlapping. project-updates = what happened. project-changes = what the plan now says differently. DECISIONS = implementation choices and deviations found while building.

project_updates.when: After a gate passes AND the task's manual verification steps have been run. Never in anticipation.
entry_fields: test counts: passed / failed / skipped / xfailed (skipped and xfailed MUST be 0)

project_changes.when: Any change to scope, sequencing, task definition, or acceptance criteria relative to the planning documents.
entry_fields: which planning document and section it affects
the addendum id written into that document
project_changes.requirement: Every entry MUST name an addendum that exists in the referenced planning document. An entry with no addendum is incomplete.

decisions.when: Any deviation from the spec or a phase document, and any implementation choice the documents left open.
decisions.note: This is the handbook's existing artifact (handbook section 1). Feed its contents back into the next spec or phase-doc revision.

addendum_convention.target: the appropriate section of the appropriate file in project_planning/
addendum_convention.rule: Never rewrite original text. Append an addendum block immediately after the affected section.
addendum_convention.spec_note: Handbook section 1 requires amending the spec with a version bump rather than letting sessions drift. An addendum records the drift at the point of use; a version bump remains required for substantive spec changes.

verification_walkthrough.statement: The manual-QA walkthroughs in guide/ are living acceptance documents, not release notes. The qa-stack tooling tracks the product automatically (it builds current images and seeds the current fixture); the walkthrough prose does not, so keeping it current is part of every epic's definition of done.
requirements: Every epic ships its own verification walkthrough (guide/e{N}-verification.md, added to the guide/README.md table) before the epic's final gate closes.

An epic that invalidates assertions in a PRIOR epic's walkthrough (e.g. E3 making device status real flips E1's no-status expectations) amends those assertions IN THE SAME BATCH that invalidates them, never later.
Walkthrough changes ride gated batches like everything else; a walkthrough landing outside the record loop is the failure mode this rule exists to prevent (hygiene finding F6).

R2_cross_phase_conventions.title: Cross-phase conventions

conventions.scope_discipline: The phase document's 'Out of scope' section is binding. The most likely failure mode of session-per-phase development is a session helpfully building a neighboring phase's feature, badly. When a genuine cross-phase need appears, the answer is a feature flag or a stub with a documented contract, not an implementation. If a task seems to need something out of scope, STOP AND ASK.
conventions.feature_flags_over_blocking: Where the plan notes a cross-epic wait, build behind a flag rather than idling or reaching into the other epic.
conventions.tests_as_contract: The four test-critical suites double as documentation. No later session may weaken them.
conventions.typed_end_to_end: Pydantic at every API and MQTT boundary, TypeScript on the frontend, no `any` escapes without a comment.
conventions.secrets: Only through SecretStore. Never in logs, API responses, fixtures, or committed files. .env.example documents names, never values.
conventions.formatting: Match the linters E0 sets up. Do not relitigate style per session.

universal_definition_of_done: CI green: lint, typecheck, tests, migration up/down, container builds.
Every new mutation audits; every new endpoint enforces RBAC.
INTERFACES.md updated; DECISIONS.md updated if anything deviated.
The demo fixture still seeds and the compose stack still starts from clean.
Handoff artifacts from the phase document exist and are named in the closing summary.

attribution.rule: NEVER credit Claude, Anthropic, or any AI tool in anything that reaches the repository or GitHub. This overrides any default assistant behavior that appends attribution trailers or footers.
attribution.author_identity: Commits are authored by the repository owner's configured git identity only. No co-author trailers of any kind.

push_protocol.trigger: After each FULL gate pass, and only after that gate's docs/project-updates.md entry is written.
sequence: 1. Gate passes: 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 xfailed, 0 deselected.
2. Run the task's manual verification steps.
4. Stage everything including the log entry, then commit.
never: Never commit or push a red gate.
Never push in anticipation of a gate passing.
Never amend or force-push a tagged gate commit.
push_protocol.branch: Work on a task-batch branch (e.g. e0-batch-1), never directly on main. Push after every gate so the remote always reflects the last green gate. One pull request per batch.
